title: Quantum Sensing and Hamiltonian Learning under Stochastic Parameter Evolution
abstract: We introduce the notion of stochastically evolving Hamiltonians (SEHs), which are local Hamiltonians whose coefficients are governed by stochastic differential equations (SDEs). After developing some theoretical aspects of these objects, we consider the task of Hamiltonian learning for SEHs. We reanalyse and make necessary extensions to the Huang-Tong-Fang-Su protocol, which first achieved the Heisenberg limit for Hamiltonian coefficient learning, under these circumstances. We delineate theoretically the regimes where the Heisenberg limit can and cannot be retained. Along the way we develop a few tools in quantum sensing and Hamiltonian simulation that may be of independent interest under similar settings in quantum information processing. The broad aim is to encourage the exploration of various settings in quantum information processing in which the control parameters are governed by SDEs.
summary: This paper introduces the concept of Stochastically Evolving Hamiltonians (SEHs) to model quantum systems where control parameters fluctuate randomly according to SDEs. It develops theoretical extensions to quantum sensing and Hamiltonian learning protocols, demonstrating that optimal scaling (Heisenberg limit) can be maintained provided the noise strength is sufficiently small. This advances the field by providing tools to handle stochasticity in quantum control.
main_problem: The paper investigates quantum information processing tasks, such as Hamiltonian learning and quantum sensing, when the underlying Hamiltonian parameters evolve stochastically over time.
main_result: The authors reanalyze existing protocols, showing that the Heisenberg limit can be retained for Hamiltonian coefficient learning and sensing under specific, small diffusion noise conditions.
method: The work develops theoretical tools for analyzing Stochastically Evolving Hamiltonians (SEHs), extending protocols like qDRIFT and analyzing the resulting quantum channel via expectation values over the parameter distribution.
model_or_system: The system is described by local Hamiltonians $H(t) = \sum \delta_i(t) H_i$, where the coefficients $\delta(t)$ are governed by Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs). The evolution is tracked via Stochastically Evolving Unitaries (SEUs) and the resulting quantum channel $	ext{St}(ho)$.
key_observables: The primary observables are the quantum channel $	ext{St}(ho)$ and the estimation accuracy of the initial parameters $\delta_0$ or the coefficients $\delta_i(t)$.
important_parameters: The diffusion strength $G$ is a critical parameter, as retaining the Heisenberg limit is conditional on $G$ being sufficiently small ($G \lesssim \epsilon^{3/2}$).
main_assumptions: For learning problems, simplicity is assumed by setting the drift matrix $F=0$ and assuming a constant diffusion matrix $G$. The analysis also relies on the validity of the time-ordered unitary formalism.
figures_summary: Table 1 compares the resource complexities (runtime, samples) for three different quantum sensing protocols under stochastic evolution.
paper_structure: The paper first defines SEHs and SEUs, then develops extensions of quantum simulation protocols (like qDRIFT) to handle stochasticity. It proceeds to analyze specific tasks, including single-qubit sensing and Hamiltonian learning, deriving theoretical bounds and necessary conditions for achieving optimal scaling.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it extends quantum control theory into the realm of realistic noise sources (SDEs), providing crucial theoretical benchmarks for designing robust quantum sensing and simulation protocols in noisy environments.
